title: Minimum Number of Pushes to Type Word I
statement:
A phone keypad has eight letter keys, numbered `2` to `9` (keys `0`, `1`, `*` and `#` carry no letters). Each key holds an ordered list of letters, and typing the letter in position `p` of a key's list (counting from 1) takes `p` presses of that key. Before typing, you may reassign the letters freely: every letter goes on exactly one key, and a key may hold any number of letters.

You are given `word`, whose lowercase English letters are all distinct. Return the smallest total number of presses needed to type `word` under the best assignment.
constraints: word consists of lowercase English letters
All letters in word are distinct
notes:
## Intuition

All letters of `word` are distinct, so each one is typed exactly once and every letter costs the same no matter which one it is. What matters is only how many letters land in each position of a key. Eight keys give eight first positions (1 press each), then eight second positions (2 presses each), and so on. Filling the cheapest positions first is clearly best, so the letters go round-robin across the keys. A brute force could try every way to split the letters among the keys, but the greedy fill makes that unnecessary.

## Approach

1. There are `keys = 8` letter keys.
2. Walk over the letters by index `i`. The first 8 letters take first positions, the next 8 take second positions, and so on, so letter `i` sits at `position = floor(i / 8) + 1`.
3. Add `position` to `pushes` and return the total.

## Example 1, step by step

`word = "abcde"` has 5 letters. For `i = 0` to `4`, `floor(i / 8) = 0`, so every `position` is 1. The total `pushes` is `1 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 = 5`.

(For Example 2, `"xycdefghij"` has 10 letters: 8 cost 1 and 2 cost 2, giving 12.)

## Complexity

- Time: O(n) for the one pass over `word`, where n is at most 26.
- Space: O(1).

## Pitfalls

- There are 8 usable keys (2 to 9), not 9 or 10.
- The position is `floor(i / 8) + 1`; forgetting the `+ 1` makes the first letters free.
- Letters are distinct, so their order in `word` never matters; no sorting or counting is needed (unlike the version where letters repeat).

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `keys` | number of letter keys, 8 |
| `pushes` | total presses so far |
| `i` | index of the current letter |
| `position` | presses needed for the current letter |

narration.2: Only keys 2 through 9 can hold letters, so there are 8 of them.
narration.4: Assign the letters one by one, filling the cheapest free position each time.
narration.5: Letters 0 to 7 go first on a key, 8 to 15 second, and so on.
narration.6: Typing this letter costs as many presses as its position on the key.
narration.8: The sum over all letters is the minimum total.
